title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Centralized company-wide policies and standard operating procedures covering access, change management, data governance, procurement and expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel policy, and internal templates. Serves as the canonical reference for employees and managers.
content:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a single, maintained reference for company-wide policies and operational procedures that affect all teams.
- Reduce ambiguity by documenting owners, approval flows, thresholds, and required artifacts.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and contingent workers unless a specific policy calls out a narrower audience.
- Topics covered: access & permissions, change management, data management & retention, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and commonly used internal templates.

1) Access & Permissions

Principles
- Least privilege by default: employees should be granted the minimum permissions required to perform their job.
- Role-based access: standard roles (e.g., engineer, SRE, product manager) are used as the first-level grant.
- Separation of duties: production access requires explicit approvals and just-in-time (JIT) access where possible.

Request & Approval Flow
1. Submit an access request via the Access Request form: /confluence/forms/access-request (required fields: requested resource, justification, duration, manager approval).
2. Manager approves in the HR portal (or email with cc to people-ops) for non-production access.
3. For production systems, manager + service owner approval required. Requests for >30 days must include a business justification and risk mitigation.
4. Temporary escalated access should use JIT workflow (IDP toolbox) and be logged.

SLOs & Reviews
- Access reviews: quarterly automated review. Team leads must attest to membership and privileges.
- Emergency access: log and review within 48 hours.

Ownership & Contacts
- People Ops: policy owner and access request escalation.
- Security: enforces SRM (Service Risk Model) and approves production roles.

2) Change Management

Purpose & Applicability
- Ensure safe changes to production and critical systems with defined rollbacks and communication. Applies to infra, runtime, control plane, and customer-impacting configuration changes.

Change Types & Approval Matrix
- Standard changes (low risk, repeatable): require manager sign-off and automated change ticket.
- Significant changes (schema migrations, infra upgrades, deployment of new runtime components): require Change Review Board (CRB) approval and a roll-out plan.
- Emergency changes: documented in post-facto change ticket and postmortem if incident-related.

Process Steps
1. Create a change ticket in the Change Calendar (Jira project: CHG). Attach runbook and rollback plan.
2. CRB review if change category is Significant. Include testing matrix, canary plan, and monitoring queries.
3. Schedule during approved maintenance windows unless out-of-band approval obtained.
4. Execute, monitor SLOs, and validate.
5. Close ticket with deployment notes and post-change verification.

Change Windows & Maintenance
- Regular maintenance window: Sat 02:00-06:00 UTC for non-critical infra. Customer-facing rollouts should avoid PST business hours.

3) Data Management & Governance

Data Classification
- Public: safe to share.
- Internal: company-internal but low sensitivity.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, or regulated information requiring encryption and access controls.

Storage & Retention
- Default retention for logs: 90 days (hot), 365 days (cold) unless flagged for longer retention.
- Customer workload data retention defaults are defined in the customer contract; follow data residency commitments.

Encryption & Key Management
- All Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Key management via KMS, with HSM for high-sensitivity workloads.

Data Access & Auditing
- Access requires owner approval and must be logged. Audit logs retained for 1 year by default.
- Data exports contain a data export form and approval from Legal for Restricted data.

Incident & Breach Handling
- Follow Security Incident Response runbook: report to security@redwood.com, contain, notify stakeholders, and escalate to Legal if customer data affected.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Thresholds & Approvals
- Low cost purchases (< $2,500): team lead approval.
- Mid purchase ($2,500 - $25,000): finance manager + procurement approval.
- Large purchase (> $25,000): VP-level approval and procurement + legal review for contract terms.
- Capital purchases vs operating expense classification handled by Finance.

Procurement Workflow
1. Raise a purchase request (Procure Request form) with business justification, estimated total cost, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement team sources quotes and validates vendor compliance.
3. Obtain approvals per threshold.
4. Finance issues PO; Procurement tracks delivery and invoicing.

Expense Reimbursement
- Submit expenses in the expense system within 30 days. Receipts required for all transactions > $25.
- Per diem and travel rates follow the Travel Policy section.

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding Checklist
- Security questionnaire completion (SIG or vendor questionnaire).
- Contract with data processing addendum (if handling customer data).
- Vendor risk classification: Low/Medium/High. High-risk vendors require continuous monitoring and quarterly reviews.

Lifecycle & SLAs
- Contract owner: the procuring manager. Procurement maintains master contract.
- SLA definitions must include uptime, support response time, and escalation contacts.
- Renewal: procurement sends reminders 90/60/30 days prior to expiry.

Termination & Offboarding
- Ensure data return/deletion clauses executed, revoke keys and access, and collect termination certificate.

6) Travel Policy (Business Travel)

Booking & Approval
- All travel requires pre-approval in the Travel Request form. Include purpose, itinerary, and estimated cost.
- Managers approve travel based on budget and business justification.

Allowed Expenses & Rates
- Flights: economy for trips <6 hours; premium economy or business requires justification and VP approval.
- Hotels: mid-range with secure internet; max nightly rates per city are in the Travel Rate Table.
- Meals: per diem with reconciliation via expense receipts.

Safety & Emergency
- Register travel with the security travel registry for high-risk regions. Emergency contact: travel-support@redwood.com.

7) Internal Templates & Examples

Included templates (copyable from this page)
- Access Request Template: fields for resource, role, justification, duration, manager sign-off.
- Change Request Template: change description, risk assessment, rollback plan, test cases, monitoring queries.
- Procurement Request Template: cost breakdown, vendor list, legal flags, procurement owner.
- Travel Request Template: itinerary, budget estimate, emergency contact.

Example: Change Request Template
| Field | Description | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Short descriptive title | Yes |
| Change Type | Standard / Significant / Emergency | Yes |
| Owner | Primary owner for the change | Yes |
| Rollback Plan | Steps to rollback if failure | Yes |
| Monitoring | Metrics and queries used to validate | Yes |

Governance & Review Cycle
- People Ops maintains this document and runs an annual policy review.
- Teams must incorporate any applicable changes into their local runbooks within 30 days of policy updates.

FAQs
- Who to contact for exceptions? Submit an exceptions request to people-ops@redwood.com with a justification and compensating controls.
- How are cross-team disputes resolved? Escalate to the policy owner; unresolved items go to the Executive Operating Committee.

Appendix: Contacts & Owners
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Security: security@redwood.com
- Finance: finance@redwood.com
